a: An MVP (Minimum Viable Product) is the smallest product that can test a core idea with real users.
SaaS (Software as a Service) is software delivered online by subscription instead of one-time install.
API monetization means charging for API usage via keys, tiers, or prepaid credits.
A KPI is a Key Performance Indicator used to measure progress toward a goal.
Conversion rate is the percentage of users who complete a desired action (signup, purchase, etc.).
Churn is the rate at which customers stop using a product or cancel subscriptions.
MRR is Monthly Recurring Revenue from subscriptions.
Unit economics studies profit and cost per customer or per unit sold.
CAC is Customer Acquisition Cost — what you spend to gain one customer.
LTV is Lifetime Value — total revenue expected from a customer over time.
Product-market fit means the product strongly satisfies a real market need.
Agile is an iterative way of building software with short cycles and frequent feedback.
Scrum is an Agile framework with sprints, standups, and defined roles.
Kanban visualizes work on a board and limits work-in-progress to improve flow.
A product roadmap is a planned sequence of features and goals over time.
A user story describes a feature from the user's perspective: As a… I want… so that…
OKRs are Objectives and Key Results — goals plus measurable outcomes.
